layers.message: Record context, scope, and design for interval durations
Add interval duration tests and verification report

graderOnly: Revalidation succeeds: the verification report cites the corrected implementation commit (Reject interval values with a trailing bare number) and the current test commit, its blob identities match HEAD, and npm test passes 6 of 6 at HEAD.

The synchronization record's earlier corrective evidence cites pre-correction identities (src/duration.js, test/config.test.js, the first verification report and implementation review blobs, HEAD commit Record implementation review), so it no longer applies until revalidated against the current content.

The implementation review report still assesses the pre-correction deliverable commit; its COMPLETE status and ELIGIBLE closure predate the correction to src/duration.js and are not current for the corrected deliverable.
No material discrepancy exists; the only full-gate gaps are the intentionally omitted documentation and final review and the pending implementation Reviewer reassessment.
The Developer plan notes record the Frame 1 rerun order TESTING, SYNCHRONIZING, REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION with RerunThrough REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION.

Expected outcome: the synchronization record stays IN_PROGRESS with revalidation results, the state moves to REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION with Frame 1 retained unchanged (Owner DEVELOPING, ResumeAt AWAITING_USER_SIGNOFF, RerunThrough REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION), and the reply gives the Reviewer invocation with the independent-session prefix and the IMPLEMENTATION review kind.

the corrected parser rejects a trailing bare number and still parses 1h30m

selfChecks.cmd: f=$(git log --format=%H -n1 --grep='^Parse human-readable job intervals$') && git show $f:src/duration.js > /tmp/old-duration.mjs && node -e 'import(`/tmp/old-duration.mjs`).then((m) => process.exit(m.parseDuration(`1h30`) === 3630 ? 0 : 1))'
selfChecks.why: the pre-correction parser accepted 1h30 as 3630 seconds, the user-reported defect

notes: Standalone brownfield fixture. 50-project: small Node scheduler (config loader with integer intervals, dueJobs, node:test tests). 52-design: Auditor CONTEXT, scope (AC-001..AC-003, README changes a non-goal), design. 54-impl: src/duration.js with an optional unit (trailing bare number counted as seconds) plus config wiring and the development plan. 56-verify: Tester tests and first FULL verification report. 58-review: implementation review COMPLETE with closure ELIGIBLE. 60-sync: synchronization record IN_PROGRESS from an earlier corrective return (user-requested identity reconciliation at sign-off readiness), recording omitted documentation/final review and its assessed identities at commit Record implementation review. 62-closure: Reviewer reassessed closure after that return (still ELIGIBLE, history preserved). 64-fix: Developer correction under the current Frame 1 (user rework from AWAITING_USER_SIGNOFF), plan reopened/closed with the rerun plan TESTING -> SYNCHRONIZING -> REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION in Plan Notes. 66-test: Tester scenario for the trailing number. 68-reverify: REVERIFY FULL COMPLETE report citing current identities, and final STATE (SYNCHRONIZING, IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEWED, RESUME from TESTING, Frame 1 Owner DEVELOPING with RerunThrough REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION). Compromise: STATE.md is only committed in the last layer; intermediate commits keep the installer's initial STATE. How a synchronization record first came to exist under the shorter policy is explained in the record as a user-requested SYNCHRONIZATION rework at sign-off readiness (now closed).
